chrome.metaDescription: Handbook and documentation for how teams screen supplier lists and validate margin with Auto-margin.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: This guidebook is a working reference for Auto-margin users. It explains how the tool evaluates a vehicle, what input data produces reliable results, and how to interpret the output.
overview.metaDescription: Working reference for Auto-margin users covering overview, input quality, dealer outreach, and vehicle evaluation.
overview.howToUseOptimallyItem: How to use optimally - required and recommended input data, the evaluation workflow, and how to read results.
overview.findDealersItem: Find dealers - applicable to users conducting B2B outreach. Skip if selling direct to end customers.
overview.isMyCarGoodItem: Is my car good? - a decision framework for evaluating individual vehicles.
overview.corePrincipleBody: Auto-margin compares the vehicle being evaluated against live listings in a selected target market. The output is a market price band, a confidence level based on the number of comparable listings found, and - when an asking price is provided - a margin estimate.
overview.corePrinciplePoint1: The quality of the output depends directly on the quality of the input. Incomplete vehicle data produces wide, less actionable price bands. Complete data produces tight, actionable ones.
overview.corePrinciplePoint2: A wide price band reflects an actual wide market spread. It is information, not an error.

howToUse.title: How to use optimally
howToUse.description: Auto-margin generates a result only as accurate as the vehicle data provided. This page covers the inputs, comparison logic, and workflow that produce reliable evaluations.
howToUse.inputDataRequirementsIntro: The fields below determine result precision.
howToUse.requiredIntro: Without these fields, an evaluation cannot be completed reliably.
howToUse.askingPriceOmittedNote: If asking price is omitted, Auto-margin will still generate a market band and listing comparison, but margin cannot be calculated.
howToUse.recommendedPowerOutput: Power output in kW or HP
howToUse.noteOnTrimLevelsBody: Auto-margin filters comparable listings using mid-tier and higher trims only, such as R-Line, AMG Line, M Sport, Style, or Sportline. Lower trims are not used as hard filters because a higher trim can be priced equivalently to or below a lower trim depending on configuration.
howToUse.comparisonLogicIntro: Auto-margin matches the input vehicle against listings using:
howToUse.equipmentFlagsIntro: When present, four equipment flags are also applied:
howToUse.fewComparablesNote: If a result returns few comparable listings, equipment flags or a less common trim may be narrowing the comp pool. Removing one flag and re-running can widen the pool.
howToUse.workflowPrepareInput: Prepare the input. Normalize fields to a consistent format. Use a single currency. Use kilometers and either kW or HP consistently across the list.
howToUse.workflowSelectTargetMarket: Select the target market. Choose the country or region where the vehicle will be sold, not where it is sourced.
howToUse.workflowRunEvaluation: Run the evaluation. Auto-margin retrieves comparable live listings, calculates the market price band, and returns a margin estimate against the asking price.
howToUse.workflowReviewResult: Review the result. Check the market price band, confidence level, and margin estimate where asking price was provided.
howToUse.workflowDecide: Decide. Use the Is my car good? page as the decision framework.
howToUse.readingResultsPriceBand: The price band, not the midpoint, is the result.
howToUse.readingResultsOutliers: Outliers are excluded from the band where detected.
howToUse.readingResultsMargin: Margin estimates apply typical market costs. User-specific costs must be added separately.
howToUse.fileAndLanguageSupportBody: The Auto-margin ingestion engine supports a range of file formats and languages. If an upload fails or returns unexpected results, retry the upload first. If the error persists, rename column headers to standard English equivalents such as price, mileage, and first_registration and retry.

findDealers.title: Find dealers
findDealers.description: This section applies to users conducting B2B outreach to other dealers. Users selling directly to end customers can skip this page.
findDealers.intro: After a vehicle has been evaluated, the next step is identifying which dealers are most likely to buy it. Auto-margin supports this prioritization.
findDealers.segmentFit: Segment fit: the dealer historically sells this class of vehicle.
findDealers.inventoryGap: Inventory gap: the dealer's current stock is structurally low in this segment.
findDealers.geographicFit: Geographic fit: logistics are workable and local demand supports the vehicle.
findDealers.priceBandFit: Price band fit: the asking price falls within the dealer's typical operating band.
findDealers.outreachBeginWithShortDealers: Begin with dealers who are short in the relevant segment.
findDealers.outreachPrioritizeHighTurnover: Prioritize dealers with high turnover or consistent replenishment activity.
findDealers.outreachLeadWithEvidence: Lead with evidence rather than description: the inventory gap, the comparable market band, and the segment match.
findDealers.outreachNoteStructureIntro: Outreach messages perform better when concise and specific.
findDealers.outreachVehicleSummary: Vehicle summary: year, model, trim, mileage, key options
findDealers.outreachAskingPrice: Asking price alongside the comparable market band as a range
findDealers.outreachFitRationale: Fit rationale: the specific reason the vehicle suits this dealer
findDealers.outreachNextAction: Next action: call, hold, reserve, or pass

isMyCarGood.title: Is my car good?
isMyCarGood.description: A decision framework for evaluating an individual vehicle.
isMyCarGood.decisionFrameworkIntro: A strong deal clears all four criteria. A workable deal clears three. Two or fewer indicates the deal requires further investigation or should be passed.
isMyCarGood.margin: Margin: sufficient spread remains after fees, transport, reconditioning, and operational costs.
isMyCarGood.confidence: Confidence: enough comparable listings support the price band to make the read reliable.
isMyCarGood.velocity: Velocity: the segment is currently active in the target market.
isMyCarGood.risk: Risk: no significant red flags in spec, mileage, history, or market volatility.
isMyCarGood.redFlagAskingPriceMissing: Asking price missing or inconsistent with described condition
isMyCarGood.redFlagAskingAtOrAboveMidpoint: Asking price at or above market midpoint before added costs
isMyCarGood.greenFlagStableComparables: Stable comparable listings across multiple sources
isMyCarGood.greenFlagAskingBelowLowerEdge: Asking price below the lower edge of the market band
isMyCarGood.knownLimitationsIntro: Auto-margin's comparison engine is reliable across most evaluations, but some results may still be imprecise.
isMyCarGood.limitationModelYearAmbiguity: Model-year ambiguity. Facelifts or new generations with the same name and power output can pull in listings from the wrong generation.
isMyCarGood.limitationSourceListingErrors: Source listing errors. Human-entered mistakes in source platforms can pass through if they are not detectable during ingestion.
isMyCarGood.incorrectResultGuidance: If a result appears incorrect, use the Copy info button and include the copied vehicle information, the processing date, and a short description of what appears wrong.
isMyCarGood.scopeBody1: Auto-margin evaluates whether a vehicle represents a good deal at the point of purchase: market price band, margin, comparable listings, and risk indicators in the target market.
isMyCarGood.scopeBody2: It does not currently predict how an individual vehicle will perform on a specific dealer's lot. The final purchase decision rests with the user.

autoForwarding.title: Auto forwarding
autoForwarding.description: Set up automatic forwarding so new deals sent to your inbox are routed to Auto-margin for validation checks. This keeps your workflow fast and consistent across the team.
autoForwarding.beforeDedicatedForwardingAddress: Use a dedicated forwarding address (e.g. deals@your-company.com → Auto-margin)
autoForwarding.beforeForwardOnlyWhatYouNeed: Forward only what you need (use rules/filters to avoid noise)
autoForwarding.beforeItApproval: If your organization blocks auto-forwarding, your IT team may need to approve it
autoForwarding.outlookStep1: Open Outlook on the web and go to Settings
autoForwarding.outlookStep3: Create a new rule (for example: Subject contains “Offer” or Sender is “supplier@…”)
autoForwarding.outlookStep4: Set the action to Forward to the Auto-margin intake address
autoForwarding.outlookStep5: Save the rule and send a test email to confirm forwarding works
autoForwarding.outlookTip: Tip: keep rules narrow (supplier list senders, auction notices, or a specific alias) to reduce false submissions.
autoForwarding.gmailStep1: In Gmail, open Settings → See all settings
autoForwarding.gmailStep3: Add the Auto-margin intake email as a forwarding address (Gmail may require verification)
autoForwarding.gmailStep4: Create a filter: Settings → Filters and Blocked Addresses → Create a new filter
autoForwarding.gmailStep5: Choose conditions (sender, subject keywords, has attachment, etc.)
autoForwarding.gmailStep6: Select Forward it to and pick the intake address
autoForwarding.gmailTip: Tip: use labels + filters so your team can audit what was forwarded.
autoForwarding.iCloudMailBody1: iCloud Mail does not support the same enterprise-grade auto-forwarding rules as web clients. For reliable auto-forwarding, set up the rule in your mailbox provider (Outlook or Gmail) instead.
autoForwarding.iCloudMailBody2: If you only need manual forwarding: open an email → Forward → enter the intake address.
autoForwarding.afterParseEmail: We parse the email content and attachments (when applicable)
autoForwarding.afterExtractVehicleData: We extract vehicle data (or prompt for missing fields)
autoForwarding.afterRunScreening: We run screening and return a result you can act on

uploadingFiles.title: Uploading files
uploadingFiles.description: Which file types we accept for vehicle lists, which we refuse, and why the list of refusals is as long as it is.
uploadingFiles.whyWeAreStrictBody1: Every file you send us arrives from a third party — a supplier, a trader, a marketplace export, a forwarded email. That is exactly the path attackers use to reach dealer systems, and a stock list is an unusually convincing disguise. Nobody thinks twice about opening a spreadsheet from a supplier.
uploadingFiles.whyWeAreStrictBody2: So we accept a deliberately small set of formats. If a format can carry code, hide its contents, or cannot be inspected, we refuse it — even when the specific file is certainly harmless. Keeping the list short is what makes it enforceable.
uploadingFiles.uploadFlowTitle: How an uploaded file is handled
uploadingFiles.uploadFlowDesc: A file you upload is checked for its type, its size and its contents. Files that pass are parsed into your stock list. Files that fail are rejected and deleted, and you are told which check failed.
uploadingFiles.uploadFlowParsedSub: You see it in the platform
uploadingFiles.uploadFlowRejectedSub: You are told which check failed

csv.note: Preferred. Smallest, fastest to process, nothing hidden inside it.

xlsx.note: The modern Excel format. Must not contain macros.

pdf.note: Dealer offer sheets and printed stock lists.

txt.note: Tab- or semicolon-separated exports from older DMS systems.

uploadingFiles.sizeLimitNote: Files are accepted up to 25 MB each. If your export is larger than that, it is almost always because it contains images — export again without them, or split the list.
uploadingFiles.whatWeDoNotAcceptIntro: The list below is long on purpose. Most of these formats are years or decades past the point where anyone should still be sending them, and several are refused precisely because they are obsolete: little modern tooling can safely inspect them any more.

macroEnabledOffice.heading: Macro-enabled Office files
macroEnabledOffice.reason: These formats exist specifically to carry executable code. A macro runs as soon as someone enables content, which makes them the most common delivery method for office-targeted malware. There is no version of a car list that needs a macro.

legacyOfficeBinaries.heading: Legacy Office binaries
legacyOfficeBinaries.reason: The pre-2007 OLE2 container hides embedded objects and streams that are hard to inspect reliably. It has a long history of parser vulnerabilities, and modern tooling has largely stopped hardening it. Open the file and re-save it as .xlsx or .csv.

legacyObscureSpreadsheets.heading: Legacy and obscure spreadsheet formats
legacyObscureSpreadsheets.reason: Formats from the Lotus, Quattro Pro and dBase era, plus interchange formats that predate any security model. SYLK in particular is still actively abused because it executes commands while looking like a harmless text file.

executablesInstallersScripts.heading: Executables, installers and scripts
executablesInstallersScripts.reason: Nothing in this category is a vehicle list. If one arrives, it is either a mistake or an attack, and we treat both the same way.

archivesAndDiskImages.heading: Archives and disk images
archivesAndDiskImages.reason: An archive hides its contents until it is opened, can be crafted to expand into far more data than it claims, and can be encrypted so that nothing can inspect it. Send the spreadsheet itself rather than a container holding it.

shortcutsRegistryHelp.heading: Shortcuts, registry and help containers
shortcutsRegistryHelp.reason: These look inert and are not. Each one can point at or carry something that runs on the machine that opens it.

markupAndVector.heading: Markup and vector formats that can carry script
markupAndVector.reason: HTML and SVG can both embed JavaScript, and RTF has been the vehicle for a long series of document exploits. If your export produces one of these, convert it before sending.

encryptedOrPasswordProtected.heading: Encrypted or password-protected files
encryptedOrPasswordProtected.reason: A file we cannot open is a file we cannot check. This applies even when the password is sent separately, and it applies to protected .xlsx and .pdf files as well as encrypted archives.

uploadingFiles.renamingDoesNotHelp: Renaming a file does not help
uploadingFiles.renamingDoesNotHelpBody: We check what a file actually is, not what it is called. Renaming stock.xlsm to stock.xlsx gets it refused at the same step, and renaming an archive to .csv gets it refused faster. If your system can only export a format we refuse, open it once and save a clean copy as .csv or .xlsx.
uploadingFiles.noteOnSpreadsheetFormulasBody: A cell that begins with =, +, - or @ is treated as a formula by Excel, and a hostile one can run a command on whoever opens the file. This is worth knowing in both directions: we neutralise those cells on the way in, and you should be wary of any supplier list you open directly rather than through the platform.
uploadingFiles.beforeOneListPerFile: One list per file. Combined workbooks are harder to reconcile.
uploadingFiles.beforeKeepHeaderRow: Keep the header row. Column names are how we map your fields, and a list without them takes longer to onboard.
uploadingFiles.beforeRemovePassword: Remove password protection. A protected file is refused even if you send the password.
uploadingFiles.beforeSendFileItself: Send the file itself, not a zipped copy of it, and not a screenshot of it.
uploadingFiles.ifRejectedBody1: You will be told which check the file failed, so you can fix it and send it again. Rejected files are not stored, not opened, and not forwarded to anyone — they are discarded at the point of refusal.
uploadingFiles.ifRejectedBody2: If you believe a file was refused wrongly, or your system can only produce a format that is not on the accepted list, contact us and we will work out an ingestion route that does not require you to change your process.
